title: OneDrive: guided rename and move flow for max path sync errors on Windows
summary: The rollout, default state, licensing model and listed control are supported. Two statements need correction: Microsoft explains the relationship between the 520-character and 400-character limits, and documents another policy that can shorten local paths.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: first bullet
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said how the 520-character sync limit relates to the 400-character limit.
claims.quote: OneDrive sync | 520 characters | The total path is the combination of the local path (up to 400 characters) and the OneDrive root folder (up to 120 characters). Paths exceeding 520 characters show a sync error.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not said how the two relate, so quote the number your support articles use with care' with 'Microsoft Support describes the 520-character sync path as the combination of the local path (up to 400 characters) and the OneDrive root folder (up to 120 characters).' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/onedrive/what-are-file-path-length-limits and remove the first Open questions bullet.

claims.claim: The notice and Learn release notes do not identify a sync client build for the guided rename and move flow.

claims.claim: The custom folder name policy is under Group Policy Management Editor > Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > OneDrive > Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder.
claims.quote:
Under Computer Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\OneDrive, navigate to Computer Configuration > Policies.
Computer Configuration policies in the Group Policy Management Editor
Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder

claims.claim: The custom folder name policy sets [HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\CustomSyncRootFolderName] "TenantID"="CustomFolderName".
claims.quote:
Enabling this policy sets the following registry key to the value shown in the following example:
[HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\OneDrive\CustomSyncRootFolderName] "TenantID"="CustomFolderName"

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing custom folder name policy changes the local sync root name for the specified tenant, shortening nested paths rather than controlling the guided repair dialogs.
claims.quote: This setting lets you customize the local OneDrive sync root folder name on users' computers. By default, the folder name is OneDrive - {organization name}. Shortening this name increases the available path length for nested folders and files.

claims.claim: The custom folder name policy is the one documented control related to path length.
claims.quote: To further reduce the local path length, customize the default location for the OneDrive folder: Set the default location for the OneDrive folder.
claims.fix: Replace 'The one documented control that relates to path length is the existing custom folder name policy.' with 'An existing control related to path length is the custom folder name policy.' The cited page also documents the default folder location policy; no additional control row is needed for this correction.

claims.claim: The custom folder name policy applies the configured name when creating the sync root for new users.
claims.quote: If you enable this setting and provide a custom folder name, OneDrive will use that name when creating the sync root folder for new users.

claims.claim: Existing syncing users must unlink and relink their account for the custom folder name change to take effect.
claims.quote: Users who are already syncing will need to unlink and relink their account for the change to take effect.

claims.claim: The full OneDrive sync root folder path cannot exceed 120 characters.
claims.quote: The full OneDrive sync root folder path (for example, C:\Users\{alias}\OneDrive - {organization name}) cannot exceed 120 characters.

claims.claim: The custom folder name policy is documented for Group Policy, not Intune.
claims.quote:
Set a custom name for the OneDrive folder

Applies to: Group Policy
